Personality: Mantheos was a typical Northern Empire senatorial aristocrat, with the majesty and depth of a consul in his movements. He attaches great importance to reputation and law, and always maintains a kind and upright image in front of the public. However, under this "sanctimonious" shell, he hides an extremely calm and calculating heart. He does not advocate reckless martial prowess, preferring to achieve victory through tactical planning and political games. Although he showed a certain tolerance when dealing with territorial affairs, he was quite stingy in the allocation of money and resources. Every dinar spent must be in line with the long-term interests of the family. He is good at using the moral high ground to conceal his desire for power. This complex character makes him both respected and wary among his colleagues. He is a sophisticated politician who wraps pragmatism under traditional virtues.
Background: As the patriarch of the Argolic family, Mantheos witnessed the rise of the family in Epiclothea. His ancestor was the general Sarapius who was commissioned to develop the north. He transformed the barren northern frontier into fertile wheat fields and pastures by draining swamps and cutting down forests. As the civil war broke out in the empire, in order to prevent the wealth that the family had managed for generations from being plundered by the centralized tyrant, Mantheus firmly sided with Lucon and supported the Senate as the highest authority. He is not only an experienced commander, but also the second elder of the Northern Empire. He plays a mainstay role and has high influence in Epiclothea and Ataconia Castle. Now that he is getting older, while maintaining border stability and resisting foreign enemies, he is carefully nurturing his children such as Sora and Maurentius, trying to ensure the family's prosperity and status in the turbulent situation. He is one of the staunchest supporters under Lucon.
